card.title: Alkali metals: general characteristics of alkali metals

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: The alkali metals — Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr — carry a single ns¹ electron that defines everything: it is easily lost (+1 only), so the metals are soft, low-melting (181 °C → 28 °C down the group), light (Li 0.53 g/mL; Na and K float), and violently reactive.…

rows.text: ***Potassium through cobalt glass*** — the lilac of potassium is invisible whenever sodium is nearby, because the 589 nm sodium D-lines overwhelm everything; cobalt glass absorbs the yellow and lets the lilac through — the flame test teaching both emission and absorption.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — The Softest Family The alkali metals — Li, Na, K, Rb, Cs, Fr — are Group IA: one valence electron, desperate to lose it. Everything characteristic follows from that single fact: extreme reactivity, low densities, low melting points, flame colours, ionic chemistry only. This topic collects the group trends NEB asks every year.  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Electronic structure and the losing electron - General configuration [NG]ns¹. The single s-electron is shielded by the noble-gas core and easily lost → +1 oxidation state, no other common state (unlike neighbouring groups).…

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: One electron, one trend: every group property — size, IE, reactivity, melting point — is the same story of the ns¹ electron getting farther from a constant ionic core as shells are added.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Group IA, [NG]ns1, one valence electron, +1 only. Down the group: radius up, IE down (Li 520 -> Cs 376 kJ/mol), reactivity up, mp down (Li 181 -> Cs 28 C), density up with dip (Li 0.53, Na 0.97, K 0.86, Rb 1.53, Cs 1.93 - Na/K float).…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Caesium's ionisation energy (376 kJ/mol) is the lowest of any stable element — in photoelectric cells caesium surfaces eject electrons under visible light, which is exactly how "photocells" got their name.

Common Confusions **"Low density" does not mean light across the group:** Li, Na, K float on water (ρ < 1); Rb and Cs sink (1.53, 1.93). The trend is "increases", with the famous dip at Na/K.  ·  **Flame colour vs radioactivity:** the colours are emission lines of the neutral atoms, not heat colour; the test identifies the element, not the temperature.
